title: Question to you Terrence Malick enthusiasts. I recently watched The Thin Red Line.

commenti.body: By investing, if you mean what makes it so engrossing and engaging that you can’t stop watching, I have always found Terence Mallick’s films a part of those genre films that work because of “the magic of cinema” you know. Because most movies and techniques in film can be boiled down and understood from a technical perspective but movies like Mallick’s that take such a different approach is something I cannot describe, another example I really like would be what Altman does in Nashville, because they are so many moving parts but the film just works, this might be me underestimating the brilliance of each director though.

A very out of left field gripe but it always annoyed me how this film focused on the US Army when the Battle for Guadalcanal is one of the most historic battles in Marine Corps history, the whole thing embodies the essence of the entire organization.  

However, I guess the story of US Army soldiers on Guadalcanal is less recited and the movie is solid nonetheless.

I remember seeing this as a college kid in the theater when it came out. A small group of fratty/sorority type college kids were there in the back acting excited, like this was going be Saving Private Ryan II.  A dude in his late thirties/early forties was down closer to the front. That was it besides me. From the moment it started I was transfixed. I remember mild grumblings from the group behind me and myself being completely absorbed by the film, the violence among the beauty, the patience among the chaos, the wonder among the dread. I loved everything about it. I looked back maybe halfway through and the college kids had left. It was just me and this forties dude. After it was over we both stayed for the credits and then I went out to my car in the freezing cold. This stranger came up and bummed a cigarette from me and we stood by my car and smoked in silence, digesting the film. I think he was wearing something vaguely 'Nam-ish, like his hat or something, but I could have made that up.  I  remember someone else was just as floored as I was and we didn't have to say a word to know that was the case. Not sure I said anything to him except good night after the cigarette. 

I'm not sure I answered either question; I'm just glad to hear someone else finds it amazing.

I love Malick's work because I find it poetic. I have not watched this one in many years, but I vividly recall being very deeply moved by the frequent juxtapositioning of war with nature. I felt there could be no better way to illustrate the senselessness of war.

Sorry, does that really matter, except in terms of historical accuracy? In a Napoleonic movie, whether it's *Moyenne Garde* or *Jeune Garde* doesn't matter very much, does it?

I think such an uncritical acceptance of militaristic culture is at odds with the themes of the movie. I know no war movie is truly anti-war, but this one seemed at least ambivalent about the value of it.
There's a youtuber called Learning About Movies who is a big Mallick fan and has a video called *The Thin Red Line -- What Makes This Movie Great? (Episode 156).* Might be worth a watch for you.

What makes it so magic is the tall blowing grass, the long crane shots, the VO, the music, the beautiful faces, the impossible sad nature of battle portrayed in this beautiful film. It's a battle of man vs man and nature is there to witness to survive to move on while man kills, burns, dies.

Back during its Oscar push I remember another director describing this movie and sorry I dont remember the director.  Essentially he was saying that if this movie was on a loop you could start watching at any point, pick it up and be immersed as it really has no start or ending.  Which I always felt was an interesting way to describe a movie.
Yes exactly, i think you answered it perfect.
I almost agree 100% with this observation. The Thin Red Line definitely qualifies. Some of TM's movies have been harder for me to get into, but this one (and many others) is a brilliant movie.
Matters to me, great thing about movies is that you can decide for yourself.  But like I said it’s a solid movie that I enjoyed watching nonetheless.
